doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Father the baseball player and practicing behind the scoreboard
summary: His father wanted him to play baseball; Bert practiced between innings and his father accepted it when he joined Barnet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And what did your father think of that?

He didn’t know what was going on really. He was a baseball player and he wanted me to play baseball so he was a catcher and he bought the mask and the protection and anyway, he later on became an umpire. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
So I had to go put the score up, so I used to bring my horn and in between innings practice behind the scoreboard.
When I went with Charlie Barnet he finally says, “I guess you’re serious.”
Yeah. He finally saw that there might be a future in this, huh?
